changes: Halo: Reach is now supported in VR alongside Halo 3 and Halo 3: ODST, with per-eye stereo, 6DOF head tracking, motion-controller aim, hands and weapon, HUD, cutscenes and vibration. New title; announced rather than itemised, since no prior release shipped it.
Reach control layout: the left trigger and X are swapped relative to Halo 3 and ODST, so grenades sit on X.
ODST: VR recovers after opening a menu instead of staying disengaged until the title exits.
ODST: VR engages reliably at level start instead of depending on a gap in the camera tail.
ODST: left stick click opens the map screen while the D-pad gesture is held.
Halo 3 and ODST: the desktop window fits the monitor while the headset keeps full render resolution, and fitted menus remain clickable.
Halo 3 and ODST: the controller is retained across title transitions within one session.
Halo 3 and ODST: resolution slider raised to 8K-class with rescaled F1 tiers.
Halo 3 and ODST: mod-owned resolve, sharpening and SMAA 1x / FXAA in the eye blit.

config_policy.instruction: Replace halomccvr.cfg; do not keep the previous file.
config_policy.reason: config.cpp parses config_version but performs no migration, so any key an older config lacks silently falls back to a built-in default instead of the shipped value. fit_desktop_window in particular defaults to false while the shipped config sets it to 1, which can reintroduce the desktop-window frame-rate cap.
config_policy.shipped_config_source: The maintainer's live, headset-tuned halomccvr.cfg, copied verbatim at packaging time.

known_issues: Reach: character tags and navpoints are misplaced in 3D.
Reach: hud_curvature and hud_vertical_offset have no effect.
ODST: the first captioned opening cutscene can be black; skip that scene once.
MCC can retain multiple title modules after switching games; fully restart MCC if a level returns to the menu.
ODST brightness stays at the game default.
rebuild_note: Source rebuilds are not byte-identical because the DLL embeds compile date/time and toolchain output can differ. The published ZIP is the exact artifact validated on a second machine before release; do not rebuild and republish without repeating that validation.
